_description: Pillar 4 — Mandatory-files (per-pillar rule model). Loaded by pre-write-guard.sh + post-write-verify.sh at runtime. Carries the per-file-type mandate registry (k8s ValidatingAdmissionPolicy pattern: matcher in pillar; paramKind body-structure contract in governance/file-type-contracts/<file>.json). Homes R-44 (_index.md mandate), R-59 (MEMORY.md load-contract cap, categorized C5), and R-58 (vault-writer reference — Branch 3). _rules[] is the per-pillar rule SoT.

_design_notes.consumer: pre-write-guard.sh (mandate-presence DENY + Branch 3 vault-writer-reference); post-write-verify.sh (Tier 1 auto-bootstrap + live-sync); librarian index-maintain capability
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 documentary lockstep — this pillar + governance/file-type-contracts/<file>.json + hooks move in one commit; no write-time DENY for R-37 (git commit-boundary + librarian governance-parity-audit).

mandates._description: Per-file-type mandate registry. Each entry is a `matcher` (file type + path/scope conditions) bound to its `body_structure_contract` (the paramKind resource). Hooks consume mandates[<file_type>] to determine WHETHER a mandate fires; consume body_structure_contract to determine WHAT the file's contract is. The two-resource separation follows the k8s ValidatingAdmissionPolicy pattern.

vault_writer_reference.scope: every Vault Writers/<writer>.md writer-reference file MUST conform to the writer-reference shape (the single authority for writer-reference shape is governance/file-type-contracts/vault-writer.md.json, R-58 matcher contract).
vault_writer_reference.enforcement_mechanism: pre-write-guard.sh Branch 3 (vault-writers-writer-reference-only) — frontmatter conformance DENY on schema violation against the vault-writer.md.json contract.

_index_md.scope: every non-exempt user-facing folder MUST carry a sibling _index.md
_index_md.exemption_semantics: positive-list — unenumerated user-facing folders default to the mandate firing. Adding a new exemption requires R-37 documentary lockstep updating this entry + hooks/post-write-verify.sh exemption-check + skills/librarian/capabilities/index-maintain.sh exemption-check. Exempt-from-mandate is NOT forbidden-to-exist: an _index.md at an exempt path that matches another capability's declared writes[] target (skills/librarian/capability-registry.json :: output_contract.writes[]) is writer-owned — nonconformance heals at that writer — and the index-maintain exemption-conflict arm skips it; genuinely stray exempt-path indexes still flag. The skip set derives from the registry at run time, never a hardcoded path list.
exemption_categories: external-root symlink surface whose subfolder indexes are librarian-generated, not mandate-bootstrapped (Work/)

plans-tree machine indexes owned by registered librarian writers (Plans/ — the plan navigation index, the inbox funnel index, the library topic/root indexes): librarian-generated, not mandate-bootstrapped, and not exemption conflicts
_index_md.enforcement_mechanism: structural — post-write-verify.sh Tier 1 auto-bootstrap creates _index.md at first-write to a non-exempt folder lacking one; librarian index-maintain Tier 2 sweep catches hand-created folders never written to. One-line self-exempt loop guard at hook entry prevents recursion on the hook's own writes.

_memory_md_cap.scope: MEMORY.md under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ MUST stay within the Anthropic-documented load contract: first 200 lines OR first 25,000 UTF-16 code units of the trimmed, frontmatter- and comment-stripped text (whichever first) loaded at session start; entries past the cap are dropped and the harness appends a model-visible WARNING footer to what it did load, so the loss is announced in-session rather than hidden. Per-line <= 200 chars (drift signal).

thresholds._governing_trigger_note: The BYTE cap is the governing trigger — it bites first (at ~110 entries) before the line cap. R-59 consumers gate on the byte ratio primarily; the line + char-line caps are secondary drift signals.

line_count_method._note: Count BOTH the raw line count AND the comment-stripped line count, and gate on the LARGER of the two until MEMORY.md comment-stripping is empirically verified — HTML-comment blocks (<!-- -->) must not buy unlimited headroom. memory-consolidation-run.sh Check 8 implements this.

overflow_routing._description: Cold-spill seam — documented design, not yet built. At byte-cap approach, relocate the COLDEST non-episodic entries to an on-demand MEMORY-archive.md and leave one pointer line in the index. DO NOT create MEMORY-archive.md until needed (auto-spill ships in a future version, volume-gated). The fixed section order below makes the cold boundary always knowable.
overflow_routing.fixed_section_order_note: Schema-derived 1:1 from memory-schema.json type enum; most-loaded-first. The cold boundary for overflow routing is always the tail of the coldest non-episodic section (Procedural, then Semantic); Episodic is a single pointer line to the append-only episodic-chronicle.md and is not cold-spilled.

_memory_md_cap.enforcement_mechanism: advisory — hooks/pre-write-guard.sh emits additionalContext warning at write-time when any threshold exceeded; never blocks the write. The byte cap is the governing trigger.

ordinal_position_check.rule: G1: a vault-pointer-shaped line whose START sits past the 200-line OR max_bytes fold (byte cap governs) loads invisibly — the harness truncates the index at the fold and the pointer never reaches the model. hooks/pre-write-guard.sh emits a distinct POINTER PLACEMENT ADVISORY (concatenated with any total-cap advisory into one emit) at write-time.
ordinal_position_check.pointer_shape_predicate: two-signal AND-gate (the false-positive killer): (a) NOT a Markdown-link entry — does NOT match ^[[:space:]]*[-*][[:space:]]*\[ ; AND (b) begins with a bare absolute/tilde path token after an optional list marker — matches ^[[:space:]]*([-*][[:space:]]*)?(~|/Users/|/home/) ; AND (c) contains a word-bounded imperative read verb — matches \b(Read|Consult|Load|See)\b. Clause (a) excludes standard [filename](memory/..) index entries that merely mention ~/ or /Users in their description text.
ordinal_position_check.enforcement_mechanism: advisory — same posture as the parent cap rule (never blocks; promotion to BLOCK gated on future observation data).
consumers: hooks/pre-write-guard.sh (PreToolUse Edit|Write G1 sub-check inside the R-59 cap block)

_memory_md_cap.rationale: Anthropic-documented at code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: the first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25,000 UTF-16 code units of the trimmed, frontmatter- and comment-stripped text, whichever comes first, are loaded at the start of every conversation. Entries past the cap are dropped and the harness announces it, appending a model-visible WARNING footer naming the overflow to the content it did load. The advisory makes the same risk visible one step earlier, at write-time, before the index is saved. MEMORY.md = index/read-replica; per-topic detail lives in memory/<file>.md reached via index-entry links and [[wikilink]] cross-references — the memory/rules pointer tier is EXEMPT from the corpus link-grammar conversion (its links resolve against the enumerated memory namespace, not the vault walk). The byte cap is the governing trigger (bites at ~110 entries before the line cap).

_always_on_context_budget.scope: The ALWAYS-ON file surfaces — every rules/ file that loads for the cwd, the CLAUDE.md chain (global + project), and MEMORY.md — are re-sent with every request of every session and are re-created for every subagent. Unlike MEMORY.md they carry NO platform cap, so this slot declares the convention: no always-on surface is bigger than the platform's own auto-memory cap (one unit), and the three of them together are no bigger than three units.

unit_bytes._note: ONE unit, ONE literal. Every threshold below is expressed in UNITS and multiplied by the value READ from the cited slot at render time — there is deliberately no second byte number here, so a correction to the auto-memory cap propagates to this budget with no edit to this slot.

bands._note: The same bands the auto-memory budget monitor uses, so one reader learns one scale.

rules_unscoped_aggregate.scope: every rule that loads for the cwd: all user-scope *.md + project-scope *.md without paths:
rules_unscoped_aggregate.render: contributor list (files by bytes, cumulative %) — no per-file threshold

claude_md._note: CLAUDE.md loads in full with no platform cap and the hierarchy is concatenated, so the byte unit applies to EACH file and to the CONCATENATED chain. The line cap is the documented ~200-line authoring convention and applies per file; line_bands are its absolute yellow/red line counts.

components: MEMORY.md (read from the existing auto-memory budget monitor, not re-measured)
total_always_on_files._note: MEMORY.md is governed by _memory_md_cap and monitored after every session by hooks/memory-consolidation-run.sh Check 8; this slot REFERENCES that verdict rather than measuring the file a third time. When the monitor has not run, the total is reported PARTIAL rather than silently under-counted.

hook_spill._note: Hook output over the harness additionalContext cap is written to a tool-results spill file and replaced in context by a preview plus a path. Any spill file in a session means a hook is emitting more than the harness will deliver inline, so one spill is enough for RED.

template_residue.method: type-2 HTML-block parser (harness-equivalent), never a fingerprint

_always_on_context_budget.enforcement_mechanism: advisory — skills/librarian/capabilities/context-budget-index.sh renders a read-replica and emits one finding per non-GREEN row; it never blocks a write and never modifies a measured file.
_always_on_context_budget.rationale: CLAUDE.md and rules/ have no platform cap, so any threshold here is a convention rather than a documented limit; the initial operating points are CALIBRATION-PENDING and are expected to move once the index has measured real corpora. They are anchored on the one always-on number the platform does rule on (the auto-memory cap) so the convention is derived rather than invented.

_rules.rule_text: Vault Writers/<writer>.md writer-reference files MUST conform to the writer-reference shape defined by governance/file-type-contracts/vault-writer.md.json (the single authority for writer-reference shape; R-58 matcher contract). Branch 3 DENIES a frontmatter-schema violation at write-time. R-58 is the mandate (vault-writer reference — Branch 3), home mandatory-files, category C1.
_rules.failure_mode: A writer-reference file landing without the required writer-reference frontmatter shape leaves the writer un-cataloged / mis-resolved by the librarian writers-* capabilities and the doc-amender fan-out.

enforcement_layer: hooks/pre-write-guard.sh PreToolUse Edit|Write advisory (additionalContext warning when any threshold exceeded; never blocks write)
_rules.failure_mode: Adopter writes MEMORY.md entries past the documented 200-line/25,000-unit cap; the harness truncates at load-time and appends a WARNING footer saying so, but only from the next session onward, and the bottom entries never reach the model. Without the advisory, the adopter has no write-time signal that part of their index will be invisible.
_rules.rule_text: MEMORY.md files under ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/ MUST stay within the Anthropic-documented harness load contract: first 200 lines OR first 25,000 UTF-16 code units of the trimmed, frontmatter- and comment-stripped text (whichever first) loaded at session start. Per-line maximum 200 characters (drift signal). When any threshold is exceeded, hooks/pre-write-guard.sh MUST emit an additionalContext advisory at write-time naming the breached threshold(s) + actual value(s) + a remediation pointer. ADVISORY — the write always proceeds.

enforcement_layer: hooks/post-write-verify.sh Tier 1 auto-bootstrap (creates _index.md at first-write to non-exempt folder)
hooks/post-write-verify.sh Tier 1 live-sync (reconciles contents-enum entry for written sibling files)
hooks/post-write-verify.sh self-exempt loop guard (one-line filename check at hook entry)
_rules.failure_mode: Folders without an _index.md appear as leaves in graph view; LLMs reading the folder have no orientation document; human readers fall back to filename-by-filename scanning. The mandate is structural: post-write-verify auto-bootstrap creates _index.md at first-write to a non-exempt folder.
_rules.rule_text: Every non-exempt user-facing folder in the vault MUST carry a sibling _index.md at folder root. The _index.md file MUST conform to the frontmatter contract at governance/frontmatter-rules.json #types.index AND the body-structure contract at governance/file-type-contracts/_index.md.json. Exempt paths are enumerated in mandates._index_md.exemption_paths (positive-list). Enforced structurally via the three-tier maintenance architecture: Tier 1 post-write-verify auto-bootstrap + live-sync; Tier 2 librarian index-maintain audit sweep; Tier 3 librarian index-maintain --deep opt-in semantic validation.
_rules.self_healing_capability: skills/librarian/capabilities/index-maintain.sh (R-34 self-healing boundary — mutations bounded to mechanically-derivable values; semantic content flagged for review, never auto-overwritten)

enforcement_layer: skills/librarian/capabilities/context-budget-index.sh (after-session read-replica + one finding per non-GREEN row; never blocks)
_rules.failure_mode: The always-on file surfaces grow unmeasured: they are re-sent with every request and re-created for every subagent, so growth is paid on every turn of every session and nothing reports it. Without the index, a rules/ corpus or a CLAUDE.md chain past the convention is invisible until someone reads a context report by hand.
_rules.rule_text: The always-on file surfaces MUST stay within the declared unit budget: the rules that load for the cwd within one unit in AGGREGATE, each CLAUDE.md and the concatenated CLAUDE.md chain within one unit (and each file within the ~200-line authoring convention), and the three surfaces together within three units, where a unit is READ from mandates._memory_md_cap.thresholds.max_bytes. Any hook additionalContext spill file in a session is RED. MEMORY.md is NOT re-measured here — its verdict is read from the existing R-59 monitor. ADVISORY — findings only, never a block.
